subject: Staged burst credit buydown proposal — PO and true-up details
messages:
From: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>
To: Launchly Ops <ops@launchly.com>, Launchly Procurement <procurement@launchly.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Jasmine Liu <jasmine_liu@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 19 Jan 2025 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Staged burst credit buydown proposal — PO and true-up details

Hi team,

Thanks again for walking through the launch week profile yesterday. Per our conversation, I attached a short proposal that aims to remove the blunt overrun risk while keeping unit economics predictable for Launchly as you scale (attached: StagedBurst_Proposal_v1.pdf, SOW_burst_terms.docx). High-level summary: 

- Staged Burst Buydown: Launchly purchases a pool of "burst credits" at a discounted rate (tiered by commit). Unused credits roll month-to-month for up to 3 months.
- Phased Overrun Cap: For the first 90 days after go-live we'll cap per-token overrun surcharge at 0% (no penalty). Months 4–6 surcharge phases 5% then 10% thereafter unless a commit upgrade is accepted.
- True-up cadence: Monthly invoice true-up with a per-line item showing credits consumed vs purchased; any overrun beyond credits billed at the capped surcharge or at the negotiated overrun rate depending on the month.
- PO/Payment path: We can accept a standard PO referencing SOW_burst_terms. Net30 preferred, but we can accommodate Net45 for enterprise procurement on multi-quarter commits.

Next asks from you: can procurement confirm (1) the PO name and billing address, and (2) whether the accounting team needs a specific invoice format (suppressing tax lines, separate GL codes, etc.)? If useful, Ben and I can hop on a 20-minute call with your procurement lead to lock language for the PO and the DocuSign path.

Drive-by notes: This structure is intended to avoid sudden throttles that would impact user experience while giving Launchly a chance to convert burst usage into a higher commit tier with attractive unit pricing.

Thanks —
Grace
Grace O'Connor
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
(grace_oconnor@redwood.ai)

Attachments: StagedBurst_Proposal_v1.pdf (proposal, 3 pages); SOW_burst_terms.docx (SOW excerpt)
From: Launchly Procurement <procurement@launchly.com>
To: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>
Cc: Launchly Ops <ops@launchly.com>
Date: Mon, 20 Jan 2025 10:04:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Staged burst credit buydown proposal — PO and true-up details

Grace —

Appreciate the doc and the clear bullets. A few quick clarifications from procurement before we route a PO: 

1) PO holder: Confirmed as Launchly, Inc. (billing address below).
2) Payment terms: Our standard is Net45. Can Redwood accept Net45 for the first 12 months if we execute a 6-month staged burst agreement?
3) Invoice format: We require a line-item breakout per calendar month plus an aggregated quarter total. PDF invoices, emailed to accounting@launchly.com, with invoice numbers.

Also, our security team wants to confirm: do the credits imply any data retention or additional logging? Ops will follow up separately with product questions.

If you can confirm the Net45 accommodation and provide a sample invoice layout, we can route an internal approval within 48 hours. Otherwise happy to take a short call.

Best,
Dana Kim
Procurement Manager, Launchly
procurement@launchly.com

> On Jan 19, 2025, at 9:12 AM, Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai> wrote:
> (attached proposal)
From: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Jasmine Liu <jasmine_liu@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 20 Jan 2025 10:38:00 -0800
Subject: Fwd: Launchly procurement — Net45 ask / PO layout

Ben / Jasmine — forwarding procurement's ask. Quick internal recommended position below (short bullets for a rapid reply):

- Net45: agree to Net45 for first 12 months IF Launchly signs the 6-month staged-burst commitment and agrees to auto-convert unused credits into a 30-day credit reserve rather than cash refunds. Rationale: payment float and cashflow impact but preserves commercial momentum.
- Invoice layout: provide the per-month line-item + aggregated quarter total (we can generate this from billing exports). Example layout attached in the proposal; billing ops can produce a sample PDF.
- Security note: confirm with Product that burst credits do not imply additional logging beyond standard audit logs; tell procurement security will receive SOC2 artifact separately.
- Concession boundary: we can include a 90-day zero-surcharge ramp; after that, overrun surcharge schedule is 5% month 4, 10% month 5+, up to 20% unless converted to a higher commit. Additionally offer a one-time onboarding credit (equivalent to 5% of the purchased burst pool) if they commit to a 12-month minimum by the end of month 2.

Action items: Ben to draft a one-paragraph PO-friendly clause for Net45 + unused credit treatment. Jasmine to check with Product/Security on the SOC2 delivery timeline and confirm invoice export format with Billing Ops. If that looks good, Grace will reply to procurement with the DocuSign anchor and an invoice sample.

—Grace

> Dana — reply incoming from our side.
From: Launchly Ops <ops@launchly.com>
To: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Jasmine Liu <jasmine_liu@redwood.ai>
Cc: Launchly Procurement <procurement@launchly.com>, accounting@launchly.com
Date: Wed, 22 Jan 2025 15:35:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Staged burst credit buydown proposal — PO and true-up details

Grace / Ben / Jasmine —

Thanks — procurement confirmed they can route a PO with Net45 if the SOW includes the unused-credit rollover (month-to-month for up to 3 months) and the monthly invoice layout you described. Security confirmed SOC2 artifacts are acceptable; please include a link to our security questionnaire response in the DocuSign packet.

Two small asks from ops/accounting: 

- Invoice true-up cadence: monthly (we will reconcile by the 5th business day of the following month).
- Credit rollover: we can accept up to 3 months of rollover, but any credits older than 3 months should be returned to Redwood (or eligible for conversion at Redwood's current market rate).

If Redwood can confirm the Net45 acceptance, the unused-credit rollover language, and send a DocuSign with the SOW + proposal + a sample invoice PDF, I will route our PO immediately after legal signs.

Looking forward to getting this across the finish line.

Best,
Eli Park
Launchly Ops
ops@launchly.com
